title: Turkey turns to Iran to contain Houthis as Saudi defense commitments grow
gist: Turkey is preparing to expand military support for Saudi Arabia against escalating Houthi attacks while asking Iran to help calm the fighting, but Iran may lack incentive to push de-escalation and its sway over the Houthis is unclear.

insights.claim: Turkey is preparing to expand its military support for Saudi Arabia against escalating Houthi attacks.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Turkish defense involvement raises the odds of a wider Gulf/Red Sea security alignment; watch Turkish arms and deployment announcements.
insights.quote: As Turkey prepares to expand its military support for Saudi Arabia against escalating Houthi attacks

insights.claim: Ankara is simultaneously asking Tehran to help calm the Saudi-Houthi fighting, using Iran as a de-escalation channel.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: A Turkey-Iran channel is a signal to watch for de-escalation of Gulf risk premia.

insights.claim: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Oct. 8 that Turkey is doing everything to resolve the situation through peace and dialogue and that Saudi Arabia is providing constructive support for those efforts.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Confirms Riyadh is publicly open to a negotiated track.
insights.quote: doing everything we can to resolve the situation through peace and dialogue

insights.claim: Iran may have little incentive to push for quick de-escalation, and may see advantage in letting the Houthis keep pressure on Saudi Arabia.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Do not price a fast Houthi-Saudi ceasefire on Turkish mediation alone; the Iranian lever may not be pulled.

insights.claim: The extent of Iran's sway over Houthi decision-making remains unclear, limiting the value of Tehran as an intermediary.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Mediation outcomes are uncertain because Houthi autonomy from Tehran is unknown.
